summary: The security relock itself reproduces correctly: both locks match the recorded digests, all seven new LiteLLM hashes match PyPI, the hashed installation and imports pass, and the pinned scanner reports the expected before/after results. Two verification defects remain: the evidence builder reports exit 0 when unit tests fail, and the exemption guard accepts a receipt covering the previous lock. The new receipt also publishes private session identifiers and records an observation end before its final test run completes.

findings.claim: Section J records a successful exit status even when the unit tests fail.
findings.evidence: The builder executes `bash -c "$1"` without pipefail; line 81 supplies a unittest command piped through `tail -4`. In a scratch copy, replacing the OpenHands reviewed digest with 64 zeros made that published command print `Ran 233 tests in 12.792s` and `FAILED (failures=1, skipped=2)`, but exit 0. Running the same command with `rtk proxy bash -o pipefail -c ...` exited 1.
findings.failure_scenario: An incorrect reviewed digest, failing test, or test-process error can produce a returned-output section ending in `exit: 0`. A reader or consumer using that status to assess validation receives a false success.
findings.fix: Execute the child shell with pipefail, or capture the Python process status before truncating its output. Regenerate section J with the corrected status capture and refresh the corresponding manifest hashes.

findings.claim: The rebound exemption is not checked against the digest covered by its evidence receipt.
findings.evidence: Changing only this evidence path back to `evidence/receipts/osv-urllib3-next-20260930.json` left all 233 requested tests passing. That receipt's OpenHands lock digest is `1d11bae34f09707d1ad353e24c33d25c7b004f25de9821d434e065b10969559c`, rather than the grant's `e24df8328149c921f751eb93d682b3f5b66eb4efd09bf4b053ffcfca057181e1`. After honestly regenerating the changed test file's manifest entry, `rtk python3 -B scripts/validate.py` also passed. Lines 607–611 check only whether the evidence file exists.
findings.failure_scenario: A relock updates the allowed digest but retains an older receipt. The guard passes although the cited receipt never carries the reachability review forward to those lock bytes.
findings.fix: For the OpenHands grant, parse the receipt and require an entry for the same lock path and SHA256, with the granted advisories covered by its carried-forward review. Add a regression case using the existing previous receipt, rather than only a nonexistent evidence path.

findings.claim: The published receipt exposes private coordination session identifiers.
findings.evidence: The publication-text audit found these exact phrases on line 8: `session (bc, <previous owner session>)`, `session <merge-train owner session>`, and `session <Gate A owner session>, this record's author`.
findings.failure_scenario: Publishing the receipt reveals persistent internal session identifiers and their coordination relationships, despite the publication hygiene requirement.
findings.fix: Replace the private names and session identifiers with role descriptions. Preserve public issue, commit and CI identifiers needed for verification, then refresh the receipt's manifest entry.

findings.claim: The recorded observation end precedes completion of the receipt's final verification.
findings.evidence: The receipt sets `observed_until_utc` to `2026-09-30T23:04:45Z`. Returned-output line 468 starts section J at that same time; line 470 records `Ran 233 tests in 12.800s`. A timestamp audit calculated the earliest completion under that recorded chronology as `2026-09-30T23:04:57.800000+00:00`, at least 12.8 seconds after the stated end.
findings.failure_scenario: A consumer treating observed_until_utc as the end of the evidence run receives an interval that excludes the final test results.
findings.fix: Record the actual builder completion time. If the retained value describes the latest command start instead, name that field accordingly rather than presenting it as the observation end.

claims_checked.claim: The six-upgrade control reproduces the previous lock byte for byte.
claims_checked.source: Fresh archive extraction, the documented Linux/x86_64 environments setting, six pinned upgrades, frozen export and appended wheel entries produced 1133 lines and SHA256 1d11bae34f09707d1ad353e24c33d25c7b004f25de9821d434e065b10969559c; bytes equalled the 29458b43 lock.

claims_checked.claim: The new relock reproduces the checked-in lock and pins.json requirements_sha256.
claims_checked.source: Independent reproduction added the two workspace edits and litellm==1.93.2 upgrade. Lock, check and export exited 0; 1136 output lines hashed to e24df8328149c921f751eb93d682b3f5b66eb4efd09bf4b053ffcfca057181e1 and matched CHECKOUT byte for byte.

claims_checked.claim: The published relock script performs no additional material workspace edit omitted by the prose.
claims_checked.source: research.md:260–271 documents the common environments edit; receipt method.command documents it, the two LiteLLM edits, export flags and appended wheels. These match relock.sh.txt and the successful independent reproduction.

claims_checked.claim: Only the LiteLLM requirement block changes: one requirement line, four removed hashes and seven added hashes.
claims_checked.source: Explicit diff of 29458b43 versus 6741c554219e showed 8 added and 5 deleted lines. Removing the LiteLLM block from both byte streams left identical contents, including every other requirement, marker and hash.

claims_checked.claim: All seven new LiteLLM hashes belong to published, non-yanked files of 1.93.2.
claims_checked.source: [PyPI LiteLLM 1.93.2 JSON](https://pypi.org/pypi/litellm/1.93.2/json), fetched 2026-09-30: every locked digest matched; the files are six CPython 3.12–3.14 Linux x86_64 wheels and the sdist. Upload interval matched 2026-08-09T02:16:21.033158Z through 02:17:49.646197Z.

claims_checked.claim: 1.93.0 and 1.93.1 are affected, and 1.93.2 is the first fixed stable release of that line.
claims_checked.source: [OSV advisory API](https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222), fetched 2026-09-30, lists introduced 1.93.0, fixed 1.93.2 and affected versions 1.93.0/1.93.1. The [vendor advisory](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/security/advisories/GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222) also names 1.93.2 among patched versions.

claims_checked.claim: The workflow's pinned scanner reproduces the recorded before/after scan results.
claims_checked.source: Downloaded v2.6.0 osv-scanner_linux_amd64; SHA256 matched ca69b3d3cd08f889a49dc0a383122f71cc528b83803671df5fd874d97485b108. Base scans exited 1/0 with exactly GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222 on LiteLLM 1.93.0. Explicit 6741c554219e archive scans exited 0/0 over 48 ordinary and 1 frozen entries.

claims_checked.claim: The final scanner result was obtained from the requested head revision.
claims_checked.source: Correction: an initial archive scan using symbolic HEAD resolved to 29458b43 and therefore scanned the base again. Git revision and archive-digest checks identified this; that result was discarded. The final archive used explicit 6741c554219e and verified the e24df832... lock before scanning.

claims_checked.claim: No other currently scanned lock pins LiteLLM below 1.93.2.
claims_checked.source: Parsed .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json inputs. The other LiteLLM pin is 1.102.1 in the frozen Lumibot lock; the OpenHands lock pins 1.93.2.

claims_checked.claim: The changed package preserves the static premise used to carry forward the oauthlib review.
claims_checked.source: Hash-verified CPython 3.13 LiteLLM wheel dee1b02b... contained 3113 package files and no oauthlib text matches. Hash-verified SDK/tools wheels had no LiteLLM proxy imports. All other lock blocks are byte-identical. This confirms the stated static premise, not runtime reachability.

claims_checked.claim: The requested three unit-test suites pass and detect digest drift, missing evidence and a changed lock byte.
claims_checked.source: 233 tests passed with 2 skips. Each named mutation failed the appropriate AllowedLockTests check. Correction: the first attempt placed TMPDIR inside the copied checkout and caused private-file fixture errors; rerunning with TMPDIR in a sibling scratch directory resolved those environment errors.

claims_checked.claim: Those suites detect an existing but stale receipt or an incorrect pins.json requirements digest.
claims_checked.source: Separate mutations reverting evidence to the previous receipt and setting pins.json requirements_sha256 to 64 zeros each left all 233 tests passing. Source inspection confirmed host.py:324–325 still rejects an incorrect pins digest at runtime; the missing test assertion is separate from that runtime control.

claims_checked.claim: Published verification commands reliably return failure statuses for failing inputs.
claims_checked.source: Section J returned 0 while reporting FAILED after the reviewed-digest mutation. Separately, hash-check.py.txt with an all-zero LiteLLM hash printed `NO FILE OF THIS RELEASE HAS THIS SHA256` and returned 0; it is a descriptive report rather than an exit-status validator.

claims_checked.claim: All changed files requiring registration have matching manifest hashes and byte counts.
claims_checked.source: Checked all 18 changed files other than manifests/evidence.json against its files entries; no missing registration or mismatch. `python3 -B scripts/validate.py` passed with 8605 hashed files and 177 receipts.

claims_checked.claim: Active digest registrations were updated, while remaining old-digest references describe historical evidence.
claims_checked.source: Base git grep for 1d11bae3 identified pins.json, the allowed-lock entry, manifest entries and dated research/receipt/review artifacts. The active registrations match the new digest. The stale ignore-reason pointer is explicitly disclosed in receipt limitations:17 and was not counted as a finding.

claims_checked.claim: The receipt is free of private session identifiers and its observation end includes all returned checks.

claims_checked.claim: The recorded CI failures, required-check configuration and claims about every head are independently verified.
claims_checked.source: No authenticated CI-log or branch-rule read was performed. Local reproduction verifies scanner behavior, but does not verify the cited job history or the assertion that no PR could merge.

claims_checked.source: No model request, OpenHands task, image installation or grader execution was run. These are expressly documented limitations; the review established installation, imports and source structure only.
